title: Successful timeout step
statement: Let $S$ be a deterministic machine and $A$ a nondeterministic machine, both over the Boolean alphabet, and fix a loop flag, an input word $x$, a natural number $m$, and a choice bit $b$. For a configuration $a$ of $A$ on $x$, work-tape contents $sT$ and head positions $sP$ for $S$, and a bit $v$, if $a$ is halted and its output is exactly the one-symbol word $[v]$, then one step of the clock host from the run configuration built from $a$, with yardstick head at position $m$, halts and has output $[v]$, preserving the input position, both machines' work tapes and head positions, and the yardstick tape with its head at $m$.
